chief_complaint: Uncontrolled stage 2 hypertension in the setting of chronic HIV infection, obesity, and obstructive sleep apnea.
history_of_present_illness: The patient is a 58-year-old man with a long-standing diagnosis of HIV infection since 2003, currently on a three‑drug antiretroviral regimen (lamivudine/tenofovir, darunavir, ritonavir). Over the past two decades he has developed obesity (BMI >30) and was diagnosed with obstructive sleep apnea in 2018. Blood pressure measurements most recently recorded are 159/112 mmHg, meeting criteria for stage 2 hypertension, yet no antihypertensive therapy is documented. Prediabetes (A1c 5.9%) and chronic anemia have been present since 2008. Since 2016 he reports increasing stress and exposure to violence in his environment, and his employment is part‑time. Outpatient follow‑up appears limited (no outpatient visits recorded) with the last encounter in early 2019, suggesting gaps in routine chronic disease management.

active_problems.name: Reports of violence in the environment

past_medical_history: Prior surgical history includes an appendectomy in 1984. Resolved conditions include multiple lacerations (2018), prior full‑time employment, social isolation, and medication review reminders. No other chronic resolved diagnoses are recorded.

active_medications.purpose: Nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitor backbone for HIV infection

active_medications.name: darunavir 800 MG Oral Tablet
active_medications.purpose: Protease inhibitor component of HIV antiretroviral regimen

active_medications.name: ritonavir 100 MG Oral Capsule
active_medications.purpose: Pharmacokinetic booster for darunavir in HIV therapy

social_determinants: Part‑time employment, recent exposure to community violence, ongoing stress, high school education level, and limited documented outpatient follow‑up suggest socioeconomic constraints that may affect medication adherence and access to preventive care.
risk_factor_summary: Blood pressure: 159/112 mmHg (stage 2 hypertension). BMI data missing; obesity documented. A1c 5.9% (prediabetic). eGFR, lipid panel, and LDL are unavailable. Charlson comorbidity index = 1; clinical complexity = moderate. Comorbidity flags: anemia present. Organ systems at elevated risk: cardiovascular (hypertension, obesity, OSA), metabolic (prediabetes, possible dyslipidemia), renal (potential HIV‑associated nephropathy, hypertension), hematologic (anemia), immunologic (HIV), and psychosocial (stress, violence exposure).

data_quality_flags.issue: BMI value missing despite documented obesity.
Renal function (eGFR) not recorded; important for HIV and hypertension management.
Lipid panel missing; cardiovascular risk assessment incomplete.
No outpatient visits documented despite multiple chronic conditions.
No antihypertensive therapy listed despite stage 2 hypertension.

clinical_impression: Middle‑aged man with chronic HIV infection on stable ART, but with uncontrolled stage 2 hypertension, obesity, obstructive sleep apnea, prediabetes, and anemia. Psychosocial stressors and limited outpatient engagement compound the risk of cardiovascular, renal, and metabolic complications. Significant gaps in documentation and management (missing labs, no antihypertensive therapy) highlight the need for comprehensive chronic disease review and targeted interventions.
